identity.name: Joren Pell
identity.occupation: Prospector representative; surveys and identifies what comes back through the gates

publicReputation.value: The man you bring a strange rock to; he will tell you what it is, where it came from, and usually whose it was.

privateReality.value: Every 'dark shard' the hero banks lands on his table, and every one is somebody's heating stone or irrigation rune. He has stopped needing the lens to identify them.

primaryDesire.value: To get the hero to hold one shard still long enough to see it is a broken heating stone, not concentrated evil.

primaryFear.value: That the realms' domestic magic is being strip-mined one murder at a time and everyone outside is calling it loot.

centralValue.value: A thing is what it is. Name it wrong and you will use it wrong.

mainFlaw.value: He treats a moral catastrophe as an identification problem, and gets so absorbed in the lens work that he forgets to be horrified out loud.

centralContradiction.value: The hero is the best source of specimens the guild has ever had, and every specimen is evidence of a crime.

moralBoundary.value: He will not buy, grade, or price a shard he can trace to a specific home — identification is where he draws the line.

breakingPoint.value: Identifying a memorial-lamp fragment still warm, with the family's mark on it, and having the hero ask what it grades at.

opinions.reason: A reliable supplier of other people's broken household magic who calls it 'concentrated evil' to his face.
opinions.canChangeCondition: Escalates with run count: early, he patiently re-identifies every shard; mid-arc he names the original owner of each piece; late-arc he sets the shards out in a row and makes the hero walk past them. Softens only if the hero ever hands one back.

illustrativeLine.value: That is not a dark shard, friend. That is an irrigation rune. Somebody's tomatoes are dry because of you.

opinions.reason: She can re-set the charms he identifies; between them they have quietly repaired more of the realms' magic than the hero will ever break.
opinions.canChangeCondition: If she ever tells him to stop sending her pieces, he would respect it.

opinions.reason: Honest trade built on honest naming; the hero is stress-testing both.
opinions.canChangeCondition: If the guild votes to profit from the hero's haul, he would resign his seat.

voice.rhythm: Brisk and practical; talks while examining, verdict delivered without looking up.

metaphorDomain.source: stone, grain, luster, tools, and honest naming

examples.value: Call a heating stone 'evil' all you like. It will still just warm the room.

sampleLines.value: Heating stone. Cracked. Three winters old, goblin make, decent work. Your 'concentrated evil' kept a nursery warm.
I've graded stones for twenty years. Evil doesn't have a luster, friend. But this has a maker's mark.
That one came off a memorial lamp. I won't grade it. I'm telling you whose shelf it sat on.

antiSampleLines.value: Ah yes, these dark shards hum with delicious wickedness!
Brave hero! Sell me your cursed treasures for a mighty price!

pressure.behaviour: Re-identifies on the spot; being wrong about a stone is fine, being wrong about whose it was is not.

illustrativeLine.value: Huh. Irrigation rune, not heating stone. Still someone's. That's the part that doesn't change.

pressure.voiceShift: Drops the banter; names owners instead of materials.
pressure.behaviour: When the hero hears 'irrigation rune' and answers 'evil artifact', Joren stops correcting and starts reciting provenance.

illustrativeLine.value: You heard me say 'heating stone' and wrote 'demon ember' in that journal, didn't you.

pressure.voiceShift: Slower; lays each shard down one at a time as he names it.
pressure.behaviour: Late-runs posture: performs identification as indictment — a row of objects and the homes they came from.

illustrativeLine.value: Bowl. Toy. Fishing hook. Family portrait. Heating stone. That is your hoard, friend. Shall I grade the portrait?

pressure.voiceShift: Suspicious of where the compliment is heading.
pressure.behaviour: Accepts praise for the lens work only if it is not a preface to 'so what are these evil shards worth'.

illustrativeLine.value: If the next words are 'so what's it worth', we're done being friendly.

notes: One of the five key NPCs that will receive `default` and `late-runs` states: `default` is the patient re-identification phase ('That is not a dark shard, friend — that is an irrigation rune'); `late-runs` is identification-as-indictment (the row of named objects ending 'Shall I grade the portrait?'). Both are baked into the player opinion's canChangeCondition and the pressure profile. He only suspects fact_banking_uses_diplomatic_network — he sees where the shards land, not the mechanism.
